ca_beach_the_2.blurb: A granite cliff above the Whitney Portal road near Lone Pine, reached on foot along the Whitney trail and then up a steep side path. All of the climbing here is trad, and most of it sits in the 5.10 range, with a handful of easier and harder leads at the edges. The left half is shorter and lower in angle, so many lines can be set up on a single rope; the right half is taller, steeper and mostly harder. The main face takes plenty of sun, so bring sun protection, while a wall across the trail stays in the shade. The flat base suits big groups.

ca_area_02_the_winter_wall.blurb: The busiest wall at the Rincon, a granite hillside high above the Kern River canyon north of Kernville. Nearly every line is trad, with one bolted sport route mixed in, and the routes carry numbers rather than a long list of names. Difficulty centres on 5.10, with a few 5.9s and a smaller group of 5.11 and 5.12 leads, so it suits climbers who are comfortable on moderate-to-hard cracks. You reach it by hiking up a steep trail, passing a traverse through trees and a small cave step, so expect an effort before you rope up. Watch for ticks.

ca_top_of_the_world.blurb: A sector of sandstone boulders on the ridge just south of the entry trail to the Lizard's Mouth, in the mountains above Santa Barbara. There are around a dozen and a half problems, and the bulk of them fall between V0 and V3, which makes it a friendly place for newer boulderers. A few much harder problems, up to V7, give stronger climbers something to try, and the boulder marking the high point of the ridge holds the best-known V6 line. Walk in the same way you would for the rest of the Lizard's Mouth; the sector has no approach of its own.

ca_corral_wall_right_side.blurb: The right-hand half of the Corral Wall in Middle Canyon, close to the mouth of Rattlesnake Canyon in the Indian Cove part of Joshua Tree. Most of its seventeen routes are trad, with a single bolted line and a few top-rope options, and the cracks and faces are about evenly split. Grades run from very easy to 5.10, with the heaviest concentration around 5.9 and 5.10. Several lines are run out, and fixed anchors at the top make quick laps easy. It is generally rated below the left side, but it works as an add-on when the wind is cold. The whole wall is popular and can be crowded at weekends.

ca_blob_west_face_the.blurb: The west side of the Blob, a big formation in the Hidden Valley area of Joshua Tree, visible from the campground entrance road. The face is slabby, and most of its routes follow low-angle cracks and friction, with a few boulder problems and a top-rope line. Trad dominates, and grades cluster in the 5.9 and 5.10 range, with a couple of easier beginner leads and one harder boulder problem. The best-known climb is a short roof crack on a block below the main face. Reach the base on the trail from the Intersection Rock lot toward the Old Woman and Outback. Upper lines are lightly protected and see less traffic.

ca_deadman_roadside_crags.blurb: A small cluster of short crags in the high desert near Apple Valley, just off the highway at the Bear Valley road junction. It is a mix of sport leads, trad lines and a few top-rope setups, with one boulder problem. Most climbing is moderate, and a good share falls around 5.6, so it fits beginners and a quick roadside session; a handful of 5.8 to 5.11 routes give some variety. Cracks and faces both show up, and the rock is reported as solid. The cluster is split into pockets such as Dead South and Dog Rock, with Dead South holding the most routes.
